name: D9 exact failing workbook prefix repeatability diagnostic
schedule: Each fresh worker executes the identical Ready prime followed by the first two block-9 warmups. No later W1 jobs and no measured repetitions. This preserves all per-worker cache history before the recorded first divergence.
identity: Use the locally preserved frozen W1 worker with its recorded SHA-256, and verify its original committed source hashes against the baseline Git tree. Keep the same actual engine, grammar, model manifest, reference runtime script, request flags, context, memory and normal cache settings. Record and freeze the new diagnostic controller separately. Do not rebuild or substitute the measured worker.
comparisons: Compare every replay against both historical prefixes, the two repeats within each frontend, and the new cross-frontend pairs. Retain exact wire/prompt hashes, generated tokens, first differing token and cache counters. Missing or invalid jobs, process samples or cleanup prevent interpreting the replay. Token differences are findings, not reasons to drop a run.
conditions: Sequential workers, AC power, no overlapping inference, local builds or bulk downloads. Record power, thermal and process memory through the existing sampler. The desktop app may remain open and idle with dictation stopped while its OS permission handoff is pending; retain this difference from W1. OS caches, time and unrelated desktop activity are uncontrolled.
limits: Four workers can demonstrate a repeatability failure but cannot prove universal determinism or its root cause. Equal cache counters do not prove identical cached numerical state. The diagnostic cannot qualify latency, change W1 requirements, justify discarding its failed warmup, or adopt the native engine in production. No mask/status/cache interventions are enabled.
